title: SEGAN: Speech Enhancement Generative Adversarial Network
authors: Santiago Pascual; Antonio Bonafonte; Joan Serrà
one_line_relevance: Early influential end-to-end waveform-domain GAN for speech denoising; a natural learned-restoration baseline for the benchmark.
verification_note: Fetched arXiv abstract page directly, 2026-09-07; confirmed title/authors/year.

title: Real Time Speech Enhancement in the Waveform Domain
authors: Alexandre Défossez; Gabriel Synnaeve; Yossi Adi
one_line_relevance: The Facebook/Meta 'Denoiser' model (built on Demucs-style architecture); strong, widely-used real-time denoising baseline.
verification_note: Confirmed via WebSearch of arXiv listing, ISCA Archive page, and Meta AI research page (arxiv.org/abs/2006.12847); title/authors cross-checked across 3 independent sources.

title: The INTERSPEECH 2020 Deep Noise Suppression Challenge: Datasets, Subjective Testing Framework, and Challenge Results
authors: Chandan K. A. Reddy; Vishak Gopal; Ross Cutler; Ebrahim Beyrami; Roger Cheng; Harishchandra Dubey; Sergiy Matusevych; Robert Aichner; Ashkan Aazami; Sebastian Braun; Puneet Rana; Sriram Srinivasan; Johannes Gehrke
one_line_relevance: Defines the DNS Challenge datasets/baselines/subjective testing protocol widely used as a speech-enhancement benchmark reference.
verification_note: Fetched arXiv abstract page directly, 2026-09-07; full 13-author list confirmed from the fetched page.

title: Audio Super Resolution using Neural Networks
authors: Volodymyr Kuleshov; S. Zayd Enam; Stefano Ermon
one_line_relevance: Early feedforward neural-net approach to audio bandwidth extension (upsampling 15-50% subsampled audio); foundational baseline for the super-resolution literature.

title: NU-Wave: A Diffusion Probabilistic Model for Neural Audio Upsampling
authors: Junhyeok Lee; Seungu Han
one_line_relevance: First diffusion-based model for audio super-resolution (16/24kHz -> 48kHz); relevant generative baseline for bandwidth-extension restoration.

title: AERO: Audio Super Resolution in the Spectral Domain
authors: Moshe Mandel; Or Tal; Yossi Adi
one_line_relevance: Complex-spectrogram encoder-decoder for audio super-resolution across speech and music, useful as a discriminative-model comparison point.

title: BEHM-GAN: Bandwidth Extension of Historical Music using Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Eloi Moliner; Vesa Välimäki
venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing (arXiv:2204.06478)
one_line_relevance: First reported success extending bandwidth on genuine historical gramophone music recordings via GAN; directly on-topic for Regime B (no ground truth, real historical media).

title: Blind Audio Bandwidth Extension: A Diffusion-Based Zero-Shot Approach
authors: Eloi Moliner; Filip Elvander; Vesa Välimäki
venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing (arXiv:2306.01433)
one_line_relevance: 'BABE' - reconstructs missing high frequencies without knowing the degradation model, tested on synthetic AND genuine historical recordings; close match to this benchmark's dual-regime design.

title: Diffusion-Based Audio Inpainting
authors: Eloi Moliner; Vesa Välimäki
venue: Journal of the Audio Engineering Society, Vol. 72 No. 3 (arXiv:2305.15266)
one_line_relevance: Zero-shot-conditioned diffusion model reconstructing gaps up to 300ms using constant-Q architecture; state-of-the-art audio inpainting reference.

title: Deep Long Audio Inpainting
authors: Ya-Liang Chang; Kuan-Ying Lee; Po-Yu Wu; Hung-yi Lee; Winston Hsu
one_line_relevance: Analyzes deep-learning recovery of long (>200ms) missing audio segments, systematically studying mask size/receptive field effects; useful methodological reference for dropout/gap restoration.

title: GACELA -- A generative adversarial context encoder for long audio inpainting
authors: Andrés Marafioti; Piotr Majdak; Nicki Holighaus; Nathanael Perraudin
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing (arXiv:2005.05032)
one_line_relevance: Multi-scale GAN inpainting music gaps of 375ms-1.5s using multiple discriminators at different temporal resolutions; relevant for larger-gap restoration scenarios.
verification_note: Confirmed via WebSearch across arXiv, IEEE Xplore, and GitHub listings, 2026-09-07; author list cross-checked on 2 independent sources.

title: DiffWave: A Versatile Diffusion Model for Audio Synthesis
authors: Zhifeng Kong; Wei Ping; Jiaji Huang; Kexin Zhao; Bryan Catanzaro
one_line_relevance: Foundational non-autoregressive diffusion vocoder; underlies several later diffusion-based restoration/enhancement models (CDiffuSE, DiffuSE) cited in this matrix.
verification_note: Confirmed via WebSearch of arXiv PDF and Semantic Scholar listing, 2026-09-07; author list and venue cross-checked.

title: Conditional Diffusion Probabilistic Model for Speech Enhancement
authors: Yen-Ju Lu; Zhong-Qiu Wang; Shinji Watanabe; et al.
one_line_relevance: CDiffuSE - generalizes diffusion-based speech enhancement to non-Gaussian real-world noise, a key generative-restoration baseline.
verification_note: Confirmed via WebSearch (arXiv listing + Waseda University research portal); full author list beyond first three not independently confirmed in this session, marked 'et al.'

title: Restoring degraded speech via a modified diffusion model
authors: Jianwei Zhang; Suren Jayasuriya; Visar Berisha
one_line_relevance: Modifies DiffWave's mel-spectrogram upsampler with a trained CNN to restore degraded speech toward the clean-speech mel distribution; directly relevant generative-restoration approach.
verification_note: Confirmed via WebSearch of arXiv abstract and Semantic Scholar listing, 2026-09-07.

title: VoiceFixer: A Unified Framework for High-Fidelity Speech Restoration
authors: Haohe Liu; Xubo Liu; Qiuqiang Kong; Qiao Tian; Yan Zhao; DeLiang Wang; Chuanzeng Huang; Yuxuan Wang
one_line_relevance: Unified analysis-synthesis system restoring multiple simultaneous degradations plus bandwidth upsampling to 44.1kHz; a strong multi-degradation restoration baseline.

title: Diffusion Models for Audio Restoration
authors: Jean-Marie Lemercier; Julius Richter; Simon Welker; Eloi Moliner; Vesa Välimäki; Timo Gerkmann
one_line_relevance: Invited survey paper specifically on diffusion models for audio restoration, combining model-based interpretability with data-driven performance; directly frames this benchmark's core method class.

title: Learning to Denoise Historical Music
authors: Yunpeng Li; Beat Gfeller; Marco Tagliasacchi; Dominik Roblek
one_line_relevance: Neural spectrogram-domain denoiser trained on synthetic noisy data to remove crackle/hiss from archival wax-cylinder/phonograph music while preserving musical content; core historical-restoration reference.

title: A Two-Stage U-Net for High-Fidelity Denoising of Historical Recordings
authors: Eloi Moliner; Vesa Välimäki
one_line_relevance: Two-stage U-Net jointly removing hiss, clicks, thumps, and rumble from historical analog-disc recordings; state-of-the-art historical-recording denoiser and directly on-topic for Regime B.

title: Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) - A New Method for Speech Quality Assessment of Telephone Networks and Codecs
authors: A. W. Rix; J. G. Beerends; M. P. Hollier; A. P. Hekstra
one_line_relevance: Defines PESQ, later standardized as ITU-T Recommendation P.862; the classic full-reference speech-quality metric candidate for the benchmark's Regime-A evaluation.
verification_note: Confirmed DOI (10.1109/ICASSP.2001.941023) and full citation via WebSearch cross-referencing ResearchGate and IEEE-affiliated listings, 2026-09-07; no arXiv preprint exists for this paper (pre-dates arXiv adoption in this subfield) so DOI is the primary identifier.

title: An Algorithm for Intelligibility Prediction of Time-Frequency Weighted Noisy Speech
authors: Cees H. Taal; Richard C. Hendriks; Richard Heusdens; Jesper Jensen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing, vol. 19, no. 7, pp. 2125-2136
one_line_relevance: Defines STOI, a widely used objective intelligibility metric; candidate metric for evaluating whether restoration preserves intelligibility vs. just perceived cleanliness.
verification_note: Confirmed DOI via WebSearch cross-referencing TU Delft research portal, ACM Digital Library listing, and researchr.org, 2026-09-07; no arXiv preprint found, DOI used as primary identifier.

title: ViSQOL v3: An Open Source Production Ready Objective Speech and Audio Metric
authors: Michael Chinen; Felicia S. C. Lim; Jan Skoglund; Nikita Gureev; Feargus O'Gorman; Andrew Hines
one_line_relevance: Google's open-source full-reference spectro-temporal similarity metric (MOS-LQO); alternative/complementary metric to PESQ for the benchmark's evaluation suite.

title: SDR - Half-baked or Well Done?
authors: Jonathan Le Roux; Scott Wisdom; Hakan Erdogan; John R. Hershey
one_line_relevance: Defines scale-invariant SDR (SI-SDR), correcting known flaws in BSS_eval SDR for single-channel evaluation; the standard SI-SDR definition paper needed for the benchmark's ground-truth-based (Regime A) metrics.

title: IASA-TC 04: Guidelines on the Production and Preservation of Digital Audio Objects (2nd edition)
authors: International Association of Sound and Audiovisual Archives Technical Committee; ed. Kevin Bradley
one_line_relevance: The core international standard for digital audio preservation practice (sampling rates, metadata, migration strategy); grounds the benchmark's degradation modeling and archival framing in the actual preservation-community standard rather than an invented one.
verification_note: Confirmed via WebSearch of the IASA-web.org web edition landing page and WorldCat/library catalog listings (Stanford SearchWorks, IUCAT), 2026-09-07; direct WebFetch of the iasa-web.org page was not attempted after strong multi-source corroboration, so full text of specific clauses (e.g. 96kHz recommendation) is based on search snippets, not a direct read of every section.

title: AI in Archival Science -- A Systematic Review
authors: Gaurav Shinde; Tiana Kirstein; Souvick Ghosh; Patricia C. Franks
one_line_relevance: Systematic review of AI applications and open challenges across archival science (appraisal, retention, records management); provides the ethics/practice framing this benchmark should engage with rather than assume.

title: Artificial Intelligence's Role in Digitally Preserving Historic Archives
authors: Zoë Teel
one_line_relevance: Discusses AI's role and risks in digital preservation of historic documents/archives, including cost and authenticity considerations; relevant secondary ethics reference for the benchmark's framing.
verification_note: Confirmed via WebSearch cross-referencing De Gruyter Brill journal page, ResearchGate, and DigitalKoans summary blog, 2026-09-07; DOI independently corroborated across all three sources.
